identity.title: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated PD-L1 knockout reshapes temporal transcriptomic responses to PRRSV infection in porcine alveolar macrophages.

content.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) suppresses innate antiviral immunity in porcine alveolar macrophages, and the PD-1/PD-L1 axis is thought to contribute to this immune dysregulation. This study investigated how PD-L1 knockout (KO) alters the host transcriptional response to PRRSV infection compared to wild-type (WT) immortalized porcine alveolar macrophages (iPAMs). PD-L1 KO iPAMs were generated by CRISPR/Cas9 targeting exon 2 of porcine CD274 locus, and knockout was confirmed in clone #35. After PRRSV-2 infection, KO#35 cells exhibited approximately 5-fold reduced viral RNA accumulation at 48 h post-infection compared with WT cells. Time-course RNA sequencing at 0, 6, and 48 h post-infection was then performed to characterize the transcriptional consequences of PD-L1 KO during acute PRRSV-2 infection. PD-L1 KO iPAMs exhibited downregulation of immune checkpoint and exhaustion-related genes (LAG3, PDCD1, TIGIT, TOX family) and NF-kappaB inhibitors (SOCS4, NFKBIA), alongside upregulation of antigen presentation (MHC I/II genes like SLA-2, SLA-5, B2M, SLA-DMA, SLA-DMB, HLA-DRA) and co-stimulatory molecules (CD80, CD86, CD40). Cytokine profiling indicated a reprogrammed response favoring antiviral signaling, including sustained elevation of CXCL10/11, ISGs (MX1/2, ISG15, IFIT1-3), and select interleukins (IL15, IL6), while suppressing pro-inflammatory TNF and CXCL8 across time points. Pathway enrichment analysis revealed significant enrichment of the cytokine-receptor interaction pathway. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) further identified a key co-expression module containing 1,763 DEGs that was associated with innate immune activation. Moreover, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis detected PXDN as a key hub gene connected to the PI3K-Akt signaling and natural killer cytotoxicity pathways. These findings provide transcriptomic insight into the association between PD-L1 deficiency and altered macrophage transcriptional responses to PRRSV infection in an in-vitro iPAM model and provide a basis for future mechanistic investigation of PD-L1 in PRRSV pathogenesis.
